title: Well-definedness of the face relation on G ×^P X' (partial-order axioms)
body_html:
Well-definedness of the face relation

Fix the induction data $(G', P)$ satisfying (P0)–(P2) and the induced space $X = G \times^P X'$ of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]. Recall the face relation $\preceq$ on $X$ from Face relation on the induced space G ×^P X' and its single-witness form on representatives: $$ (g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2) \;:\iff\; \exists\, n \in G',\;\; n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2 \;\text{and}\; g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}. $$

This node establishes the four theorems needed to upgrade $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ to a well-defined partial order on the quotient $X$: reflexivity, transitivity, descent through $\sim$, and antisymmetry modulo $\sim$.

Theorem 1 (reflexivity)

$(g, E) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g, E)$ for every $(g, E) \in G \times X'$.
proof_html:
Take $n := 1 \in G'$. Then $1 \cdot E = E \preceq E$ and $g^{-1} g \cdot 1 = 1 \in P_E$. $\square$

Theorem 2 (transitivity)

Under (P0) and (P1), $\preceq_{\text{rep}}$ is transitive: given witnesses $n_1$ for $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $n_2$ for $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$, the product $n := n_2 n_1 \in G'$ witnesses $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_3, E_3)$.

Face-chain. $n \cdot E_1 = n_2 \cdot (n_1 \cdot E_1) \preceq n_2 \cdot E_2 \preceq E_3$, using cellularity of $n_2$ (preserves $\preceq$) and transitivity of $\preceq$ on $X'$.

Residual. Set $p_1 := g_1^{-1} g_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$ and $p_2 := g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2 \in P_{E_2}$. Then $$ g_1^{-1} g_3 (n_2 n_1) = (g_1^{-1} g_2)(g_2^{-1} g_3 n_2)(n_1) = (p_1 n_1^{-1}) p_2 n_1 = p_1 \cdot \bigl(n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1\bigr). $$

To conclude $g_1^{-1} g_3 n \in P_{E_1}$, we show $n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$:

  • $p_2 \in P_{E_2}$.
  • From $n_1 \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$ and (P0): $P_{E_2} \le P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$, so $p_2 \in P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$.
  • From (P1): $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1} = n_1 P_{E_1} n_1^{-1}$, i.e.\ $n_1^{-1} P_{n_1 \cdot E_1} n_1 = P_{E_1}$. Applying to $p_2$: $n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1 \in P_{E_1}$.

Hence $g_1^{-1} g_3 n = p_1 \cdot (n_1^{-1} p_2 n_1) \in P_{E_1} \cdot P_{E_1} = P_{E_1}$. $\square$

Role of each axiom. (P0) lifts $p_2$ from $P_{E_2}$ into the larger $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$ along the face relation $n_1 E_1 \preceq E_2$. (P1) conjugates $P_{n_1 \cdot E_1}$ back to $P_{E_1}$ via $n_1 \in G'$. Neither can be dispensed with — a $P$ without cosheaf monotonicity or without $G'$-equivariance breaks transitivity of the induced face relation.

Theorem 3 (descent through $\sim$)

The face relation defined via representatives must be independent of the choice of representative for both arguments to descend to a well-defined relation on the quotient $X$.

Under (P0) and (P1), for $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_1', E_1')$ and $(g_2, E_2) \sim (g_2', E_2')$, $$ (g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2) \iff (g_1', E_1') \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2', E_2'). $$

Proof (left descent). Take $m \in G'$ with $m \cdot E_1 = E_1'$ and $\alpha := g_1^{-1} g_1' m \in P_{E_1}$. Assume $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := n m^{-1}$:

  • Face-chain. $n'' \cdot E_1' = n m^{-1} \cdot (m \cdot E_1) = n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$.
  • Membership. $(g_1')^{-1} g_2 n'' = m \alpha^{-1} g_1^{-1} g_2 n m^{-1}$; substitute $g_1^{-1} g_2 n \in P_{E_1}$ and use (P1) with $m$ to conclude $m \alpha^{-1} (g_1^{-1} g_2 n) m^{-1} \in m P_{E_1} m^{-1} = P_{m \cdot E_1} = P_{E_1'}$.

Reverse direction: symmetric via $m^{-1}$.

Proof (right descent). Take $m \in G'$ with $m \cdot E_2 = E_2'$ and $\beta := g_2^{-1} g_2' m \in P_{E_2}$. Assume $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ with witness $n$. Take $n'' := m n$:

  • Face-chain. $n'' \cdot E_1 = m \cdot (n \cdot E_1) \preceq m \cdot E_2 = E_2'$.
  • Membership. $\beta \in P_{E_2}$, and by (P0) with $n \cdot E_1 \preceq E_2$: $\beta \in P_{n \cdot E_1}$. By (P1): $\beta = n p n^{-1}$ for some $p \in P_{E_1}$. Compute $g_1^{-1} g_2' n'' = (g_1^{-1} g_2 n) \cdot p \in P_{E_1} \cdot P_{E_1} = P_{E_1}$.

$\square$

Theorem 4 (antisymmetry modulo $\sim$)

If $(g_1, E_1) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_2, E_2)$ and $(g_2, E_2) \preceq_{\text{rep}} (g_1, E_1)$, then $(g_1, E_1) \sim (g_2, E_2)$.

Proof. From witnesses $n_1$ and $n_2$ respectively, we get $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 \preceq E_1$. The $G$-action is cellular (Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex), hence dimension preserving: $\dim((n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1) = \dim E_1$. Strict monotonicity of $\dim$ along a proper face-chain (Abstract cell complex) forces $(n_2 n_1) \cdot E_1 = E_1$, so $n_1 \cdot E_1 = E_2$, and the $P_{E_1}$-membership from the $n_1$-witness is exactly the $\sim$-witness. $\square$

Corollary (partial-order structure)

Combining Theorems 1–4 with the descent proposition:

$\preceq$ on $X = (G \times X')/{\sim}$ is a well-defined partial order.

Which axioms enter which theorem

Theorem Axioms used
Reflexivity (Theorem 1) none (unit in $G'$, unit in $P_E$)
Transitivity (Theorem 2) (P0), (P1)
Left descent (part of Theorem 3) (P1)
Right descent (part of Theorem 3) (P0), (P1)
Antisymmetry mod $\sim$ (Theorem 4) dim preservation (cellular action) + strict monotonicity of $\dim$

(P2) does not enter this node. It is the axiom needed for injectivity of $\iota$ (ι : X' → G ×^P X' is a cellular embedding (poset form) clause (1)), not for the face relation itself.

Lean formalization

Each theorem corresponds to a dedicated Lean lemma in SheafOnBuilding.Induction:

Theorem Lean lemma Axioms used
Reflexivity (Theorem 1) InductionLe_refl none
Transitivity (Theorem 2) InductionLe_trans (P0), (P1)
Left descent (Theorem 3, ⟵) InductionLe_left_descends (P1)
Right descent (Theorem 3, ⟶) InductionLe_right_descends (P0), (P1)
Antisymmetry mod $\sim$ (Theorem 4) InductionLe_antisymm GCellComplex.smul_dim, AbstractCellComplex.dim_lt

The residual conjugation identity $$ g_1^{-1} g_3 (n_2 n_1) = p_1 \cdot n_1^{-1} (n_2 p_2^{-1} n_2^{-1}) n_1 $$ appearing in the Theorem 2 proof reappears verbatim in the Theorem 3 descent proofs and in the (⇒) direction of the definition ⇔ single-witness equivalence (Face relation on the induced space G ×^P X' Theorem 1). All four proofs are instances of the same (P0)+(P1) group-theoretic manoeuvre.

These lemmas assemble the PartialOrder (InducedSpace d) instance via Quotient.lift₂:

instance : PartialOrder (InducedSpace d) where
  le := Quotient.lift₂ (InductionLe d) <descent proof>
  le_refl q     := Quotient.inductionOn q (InductionLe_refl d)
  le_trans      := Quotient.inductionOn₃ _ _ _ (fun _ _ _ => InductionLe_trans d)
  le_antisymm   := Quotient.inductionOn₂ _ _
    (fun _ _ h₁ h₂ => Quotient.sound (InductionLe_antisymm d h₁ h₂))

The <descent proof> argument of Quotient.lift₂ is exactly the representative-independence check discharged by InductionLe_left_descends + InductionLe_right_descends.
